changes.before: Implement route(command) with match/case. ["greet", name] returns "Hello " plus name only when name is a string; ["pause"] returns "Paused"; everything else returns "Unknown". Accept matching tuples too and preserve input.
changes.after: Choose a response by matching the shape of a command.

before: match command examines a value; each case is a pattern, not a function call. The sequence pattern ["greet", name] requires two elements, matches the literal first element, and binds the second to name. A bare name in a pattern captures a value; it does not compare against an earlier variable of that name.

The guard if isinstance(name, str) runs after the shape matches. isinstance receives a value and a class and returns a Boolean; here it rejects a non-string name. Only the first successful case runs. The wildcard _ matches anything without binding a new name, so put the fallback last.

```python
def route(command):
    match command:
        case ["greet", name] if isinstance(name, str):
            return f"Hello {name}"
        case ["pause"]:
            return "Paused"
        case _:
            return "Unknown"

print(route(["greet", "Ada"]))
print(route(["pause"]))
print(route(["greet", 7]))
```
The outputs are Hello Ada, Paused, and Unknown. route accepts a command value and returns one message string; it does not change the input.

Sequence patterns also match suitable tuples, but do not split str or bytes into characters. An extra element prevents this exact two-element pattern from matching. For example, route(["greet", "Ada", "extra"]) returns Unknown. Guard failure permits the following cases to be tried.

after:
`match command` checks a value against the shapes listed after `case`.

The pattern `["greet", name]` needs two items. The first must be `"greet"`. The second is saved as `name`.

A name written on its own in a pattern saves a value. It does not compare against an older value of that name.

A guard is an extra `if` check after a pattern. Here, `if isinstance(name, str)` asks whether `name` is a string. It runs only after the two-item shape matches.

Only the first matching case with a passing guard runs. `_` matches anything without saving a name, so put that catch-all case last.

```python
def route(command):
    match command:
        case ["greet", name] if isinstance(name, str):
            return f"Hello {name}"
        case ["pause"]:
            return "Paused"
        case _:
            return "Unknown"

print(route(["greet", "Ada"]))
print(route(["pause"]))
print(route(["greet", 7]))
```
It prints `Hello Ada`, `Paused`, and `Unknown`. `route` reads a command and returns a message without changing the command.

These patterns can match lists or tuples. They do not split strings or bytes into items.

The greeting pattern needs exactly two items. `route(["greet", "Ada", "extra"])` has three, so it returns `"Unknown"`.

If a guard fails, Python can still try the later cases.
